note: Benchmark service lives for sewer pipes, by material, with their published sources: the reference for judging how old Calgary's sewers are against how long such pipes are expected to last. There is no single world figure: utilities set their own. "low" is the short end of published ranges, "typical" is a Canadian city's own figure (Saanich, 2023), "high" is the long end. Age is a guide where inspections are not published, not proof that a pipe has failed. Cite the sources listed with each figure.

Saanich 45 (unreinforced) to 100 (reinforced); Sydney Water 130; Halcrow 75 to 100

context.fact: New water, sewer and stormwater pipes laid in Canada in 2020 were expected to last 50 to 73 years.
Eight UK water companies used sewer lives from 40 to 200 years, most between 40 and 150.
Germany's public sewers averaged 39.8 years old (50 in cities over 250,000); about 1.1% of the network was renewed each year.
In Canada, 13% of sewer pipes under 450 mm were in poor or very poor condition in 2022.
US wastewater infrastructure earned a D+ in the 2025 national report card.
